scope: Qualify the existing Job 2:9 interpretation note and align active lexical/theological rationale; unchanged Hebrew, full marked main English and anchor; no whole-verse or source-priority certification
note: Hebrew literally “Bless God and die.” POB interprets “bless” here as an indirect way of saying “curse,” in light of 1:11; 2:5 and Job’s reply in 2:10. A literal blessing before death remains another interpretation.
lexical_rationale: The written verb normally means “bless.” POB provisionally renders its contextual force as “curse,” comparing 1:11; 2:5 and the reply in 2:10. Literal blessing before death remains an interpretive alternative; neither interpretation requires different Hebrew letters.
theological_chosen_reading: Retain the contextual “Curse God and die” in the main text, with the literal Hebrew “Bless God and die” and the competing blessing interpretation disclosed in the note.
theological_rationale: The source spelling is unchanged. The prologue and Job’s reply support the contextual rendering, but a literal blessing interpretation remains viable. The current main text and note must be described consistently, without treating this provisional interpretation as a settled source-text result.
